demonstrated_gap: Runs a libkrun VM per sandbox on Linux KVM, macOS Apple Silicon and Windows WHP. It adds live snapshot/fork (warm, clean workers) and secrets bound to an allowed host so the value never enters the VM. The current README documents an egress allowlist (sandbox.yaml `network: allow`; SDK allowed_hosts/allowed_ports) and cpus/memory limits, which the 2026-09-22 fit correction did not find in the evidence it read. Snapshot/fork is the axis neither srt nor BoxLite's --rm path covers. It shares the KVM precondition on the Linux host. v0.7.3 shipped on 2026-09-24, after the prior keep_but_compare verdict.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Use the same fixture and resource probes. Prefer microsandbox over BoxLite only if it matches BoxLite's enforcement results and its snapshot-restored workers cut per-task wall time well below coop's 10.9 s median, with cleanup leaving no residue.

demonstrated_gap: Addresses open gap 5 and the layer's next_action (compare srt with one OCI/VM candidate on filesystem/network/resource enforcement, cleanup and host compatibility). The only VM arm run so far (trailofbits/coop, 2026-09-23) lost the preregistered 8-probe fixture: 5/8 denied versus srt's 8/8, because coop leaves outbound TCP, DNS and guest sudo open by design. BoxLite is the first local VM runtime found that documents every axis that fixture tests, plus the axes where the layer has no qualification, in one CLI. It runs one KVM/Hypervisor.framework VM per box inside a jailer (seccomp on Linux, sandbox-exec on macOS; --security defaults to enable). Egress is either --network disabled or --allow-net over exact hosts, wildcards, IPs and CIDRs (hostname-only rules deny UDP); inbound is disabled by default and tx/rx bandwidth caps exist. Resources: --cpus/--memory plus a SecurityOptions.maximum() preset for untrusted AI code (max_processes=100, max_open_files=1024, max_file_size=1GiB; cgroups/rlimits). Cleanup: --rm. Hosts: it documents 'Windows (WSL2) x86_64' with 'user in kvm group' and macOS Apple Silicon, the host where both winners are untested. The embedded local mode is daemonless with no account, and the CLI reference documents SHA256SUMS and sigstore build-provenance attestations. The layer records no resource-limit or VM-boundary qualification for srt. Feasibility caveat from read-only host checks on 2026-09-26: /dev/kvm is root:systemd-resolve (gid 991) 0660, access(2) denies the agent user, and the user is not in kvm (gid 993). The Linux arm therefore needs an owned, stable /dev/kvm ownership fix (OS consent) first. The M5 Pro arm can run now.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Preregister and rerun the same 8-probe srt fixture (5 fresh instances per arm, as in the coop comparison) using `boxlite run --rm --security enable`, once with --network disabled and once with --allow-net. Add probes srt cannot express: a memory balloon past --memory, a fork bomb past max_processes, raw-IP and UDP egress under hostname-only rules, and residue after a kill (box, disk, process). Adopt BoxLite as the enforced-boundary lane for untrusted research code only if it denies every probe srt denies, enforces the caps, leaves no residue, keeps KVM access stable on WSL2 across the run and a WSL restart, and passes on the M5 Pro. Otherwise srt stays the sole default. Record median wall time against srt's 0.45 s and coop's 10.9 s to decide between per-command and per-task use.
evidence: https://github.com/boxlite-ai/boxlite/blob/main/README.md — supported platforms: macOS Apple Silicon; Linux x86_64/ARM64; 'Windows (WSL2) x86_64' requiring 'WSL2 with KVM support, user in kvm group'. Security layers: KVM/Hypervisor.framework + jailer (seccomp/sandbox-exec) + cgroups/rlimits. Daemonless embedded library with an egress allow-list.

demonstrated_gap: The current sandbox lacks resource-limit qualification. Podman supplies a concrete OCI comparison with CPU, memory and process controls, disposable filesystems and disconnected networking. Linux containers share the host kernel; this does not establish a VM boundary.
comparison_that_would_overturn: First compare rootless Podman on WSL2 against sandbox-runtime 0.0.77 using the same offline historical-replay fixture. Require identical outputs, zero access to outside-workspace sentinels, enforced memory/CPU/PID limits, denied IPv4/IPv6 egress, and no surviving processes or mounts after forced termination. Confirm cgroup delegation before interpreting resource results. Separately qualify Podman Machine on both Macs.
evidence: [Upstream overview](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman): documents rootless OCI execution, resource isolation, lifecycle management and Mac/Windows operation through managed VMs.

[Run reference](https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-run.1.html): documents CPU quotas, memory controls, PID limits, network=none and timeouts; rootless cgroup-v1 restrictions make host configuration a qualification prerequisite.

demonstrated_gap: Covers the same VM-tier gap with the safest default found: 'Networking is disabled by default', an --allow-host egress allowlist, per-VM cpus/memory (4 vCPU / 8 GiB default with balloon), an ephemeral `machine run` that is 'cleaned up after exit', and support for Linux x86_64 KVM and macOS Apple Silicon. It is the most active libkrun runtime (three releases on 2026-09-24/25) and drew 1 of 3 targeted votes in the prior sdk-runtime ledger. By its own security model it ranks behind BoxLite for hostile code. The VMM runs unconfined as the invoking user ('For hostile local co-tenants, add host-level account separation and OS confinement around the VMM process'), and 'Releases are not currently signed or accompanied by provenance attestations, and the installer permits installation when the checksum file cannot be downloaded.' It shares BoxLite's KVM precondition on the Linux host.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Run smolvm as the second VM arm on the same fixture if BoxLite fails on host compatibility, cleanup or latency. Prefer smolvm only if it denies every srt-denied probe both with networking off and with --allow-host, leaves no residue, still works when its VMM is itself wrapped in an OS sandbox (for example srt), and release verification becomes available (signatures or provenance).

demonstrated_gap: Provides process-tier resource enforcement the layer has never qualified: max_memory and max_processes through seccomp user notification, with no root and no cgroups. It also offers HTTP method+host+path ACLs through a transparent proxy, where srt enforces at domain granularity (per the 2026-09-22 source read), and starts in about 5 ms. It runs on the Linux host now without KVM. Kernel 6.18.33 exceeds its Linux 6.12 (Landlock ABI v6) floor, and /proc/config.gz shows CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK=y with landlock first in CONFIG_LSM and no lsm= override (read-only check, 2026-09-26). Limits: Linux only (no macOS arm), created 2026-03, 423 stars.
comparison_that_would_overturn: If the VM arm cannot hold stable KVM access on WSL2, run sandlock on the 8-probe fixture plus memory-balloon and fork-bomb probes. Compare it against srt wrapped in a native `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=... -p TasksMax=...`. Adopt sandlock only if it denies every srt-denied probe and enforces caps the native systemd scope cannot, at comparable latency.
evidence: https://github.com/multikernel/sandlock/blob/main/README.md — Landlock (filesystem+network+IPC) + seccomp-bpf + seccomp user notification; 'Linux 6.12+ (Landlock ABI v6)'; --net-allow host:port; --http-allow/--http-deny method+host+path; max_memory/max_processes; resource limits via 'seccomp notif + SIGSTOP'; startup table showing ~5 ms.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26298 — 'Sandlock: Confining AI Agent Code with Unprivileged Linux Primitives' (2026-05-25): roughly 5 ms startup overhead, Redis throughput within measurement noise of bare metal, no root/cgroups/images.
